solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I object to a certain course of action

parts.note: the objective case of the pronoun I is me, so I as a grammatical object gives ME
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a particular plan being followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' reads as a protest, but it means the word I in the objective case: ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a step or plan taken to achieve something, a synonym for a course of action.

clue.text: Pin back centre of masculine vestment

indicators.note: placed at the centre of means set inside the word for masculine

parts.note: masculine means male

indicators.note: back means the word pin is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Pinning something at the middle of a man's garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' reads as picking the middle letter of masculine, but it is a container signal: the reversed pin goes into the centre of the word for masculine.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple is a strip of embroidered cloth worn on the left arm by a priest at Mass, a liturgical vestment.

clue.text: Compensate a heavyweight Earl

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: Paying off a large nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends or reparation, to compensate for a wrong.

clue.text: Startled deer do run when not organised

indicators.note: startled animals scatter in confusion, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Frightened deer bolt in a disorderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Unordered means lacking any arrangement, the same as not organised.

clue.text: The aristocracy are regularly well-birthed

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every second letter of well-birthed

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are, as a rule, of good birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite is the select top group in society, which the aristocracy forms.

clue.text: Father, leases, with mother as well

definitions.text: Father, leases, with mother as well

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
rents means leases, as a verb

explanation.surface: A father lets property, and the mother joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: PA plus RENTS gives the word, and the whole clue describes it: father together with mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents are a father and a mother taken together.

clue.text: Flower worn by a colourful hero?

definitions.meaning: a small plant with red, blue or white flowers, the scarlet one being common
the Scarlet ... is the hero of Baroness Orczy's novels, who signed himself with that flower

explanation.surface: A flower pinned on a brightly dressed hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scarlet Pimpernel is the swashbuckling hero of Baroness Orczy's novels, named after the red wild flower; 'colourful' points to scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: The pimpernel is a small wild flower, and the Scarlet Pimpernel took it as his emblem.

clue.text: Antique contents were licensed

indicators.note: contents means the letters lie inside the words were licensed

explanation.surface: The items in an antiques shop had been granted a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, an antique.

clue.text: Tell Satan to muck out the cowshed!

indicators.note: to muck out is to clean and turn over the bedding, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An order telling the Devil to clean out the cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat-stall is an old word for a stall for cattle, neat meaning oxen.

clue.text: Convince to pay in full

definitions.meaning: to persuade someone fully, putting their doubts to rest
to settle a debt or claim completely

explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy is both to convince someone and to discharge a debt completely.

clue.text: Is 'engloom' a newly coined word?

indicators.note: newly signals the letters are made over afresh into another order

explanation.surface: A question whether the word engloom is a recent invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' looks like part of the definition but signals the anagram of IS ENGLOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word or expression.

clue.text: Lowest degree for trainee getting the point

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
east is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A trainee is given the lowest grade for reaching a certain stage.
explanation.walkthrough: L plates mark a learner driver in Britain, so L means a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means the smallest amount, as in 'not in the least', the lowest degree.

clue.text: Request quiet guide

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
to guide is to lead

explanation.surface: Asking a guide to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest request.

clue.text: Worries about assignments

definitions.meaning: to be exercised about something is to worry over it
tasks set for practice, as in school homework

explanation.definitionFit: Exercises are set tasks, and to exercise someone is to trouble or preoccupy them.

clue.text: Amuse host

definitions.meaning: to give pleasure or fun to people
to receive guests and provide hospitality

explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is both to amuse and to have guests round as host.

clue.text: Ex-PM's roofers

definitions.meaning: belonging to Margaret Thatcher, former British Prime Minister
craftsmen who make roofs of straw or reed

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's workmen putting on a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was UK Prime Minister 1979-90; a thatcher roofs with straw or reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatchers are roofers working in straw or reed, and the name of the former Prime Minister.

clue.text: A sanctimonious group of timeless artists keep bees

parts.note: pi is a short informal form of pious, meaning sanctimonious

indicators.note: less time means the letter T, standard for time, is removed

parts.note: taken as the word itself before the T goes
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A self-righteous band of artists take up beekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops a T (time) from ARTISTS, leaving ARISTS. The definition is a verb phrase standing for the people who keep bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiarists are beekeepers, people who keep bees as hives.

clue.text: Reveal you are a little immature

indicators.note: a little of the words Reveal you means some letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: Telling someone they are rather childish.
explanation.definitionFit: Vealy means like veal, young calf, hence immature or callow.

clue.text: Food the vet and beagle both chewed

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters are mashed into another order

explanation.surface: Something to eat that both the vet and a dog have gnawed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable is a plant eaten as food.

clue.text: Vegetable tea brewed by Rural Dean

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
RD is the abbreviation for Rural Dean, a Church of England cleric

explanation.surface: A Rural Dean makes a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green vegetable related to beet.

clue.text: Illustration of box containing nothing

indicators.note: containing means the word for box holds the other piece

parts.note: a carton is a box
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A picture of an empty box.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a drawing, an illustration, often humorous.

clue.text: I will, for example, collaborate feloniously

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to ally is to join forces, collaborate

explanation.surface: Someone vows to join in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Feloniously means by committing a felony, against the law.

clue.text: Badly dyed lei was cropped

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A poorly coloured garland had been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropped' suggests cut short, but here means produced as a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that cropped produced a harvest, that is, it yielded.

clue.text: Shoe carer prepared a Grand National runner

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A farrier readies a horse for a big race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British steeplechase run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand National runners are horses bred and trained for racing.

clue.text: Enraged — the Spanish find a place to stay

parts.note: hot can mean angry, as in hot under the collar
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: An angry Spaniard finds lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is an establishment offering accommodation to stay in.

clue.text: Raise the spirits of the Earl recently

parts.note: late can mean recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: Cheering up a nobleman lately.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with joy, to lift someone's mood.

clue.text: Article about a knight who was the King's companion

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the following two pieces

parts.note: the is the definite article
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on a knight who served alongside a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts THE round A plus N, the chess knight. The definition is a relative clause: a thane was the one who was the king's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was an Anglo-Saxon nobleman who held land from and attended on the king.

clue.text: Look for a delay

parts.note: to wait is to delay

explanation.surface: Searching for a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To await is to look forward to or expect something to come.

clue.text: There's nothing green, just plain

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: An unadorned field with no greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly shown, plain to see.

clue.text: The celebrity panel is on the right

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a board is a panel, of wood or of people

explanation.surface: A famous person serving on a committee is in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'panel' suggests a group of judges, but here it is a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: Little eagles start to rest in their eyries for cuddles

indicators.note: rest in means the first two letters sit inside the word for eyries

parts.note: eyries are eagles' nests

indicators.note: start to means take the opening letter of each of Little and eagles

explanation.surface: Young eagles settle into their nests for a snuggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestles means snuggles close, a synonym of cuddles.

clue.text: Created an upstanding journalist

parts.note: upstanding means standing upright, erect
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist was made with integrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Erected means built or set up, that is, created.
